summary: Every credential, including each OAuth client, gets its own local database (data-<hash>.db keyed by the same fingerprint as policy backups, set in configureDefaultDBScope before the learn store initializes); the shared data.db is never used once a credential is configured, and the MCP server's direct store tools compute the same per-credential path without shared state.
reason: The default selector '-' names a different tailnet per credential and synced rows carry no credential, so a shared database mixed tailnets in search and overwrote rows with the same ID; the generated scope hashed the raw Authorization header (empty for OAuth before minting), fell back to an existing data.db, and MCP always used data.db.
